experiments.name: reset-chain measurement
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 4294967295; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.w $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 4000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 4294967295; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.w $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'vdiv.wu $vr0, $vr0, $vr2; vpickve2gr.wu $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: Element-0 reset chain; the closure latency is cancelled by the calibration experiment.

experiments.name: vadd.b reset-helper baseline
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 4294967295; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.w $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 4000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 4294967295; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.w $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'vadd.b $vr0, $vr0, $vr2; vpickve2gr.wu $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: Same helper chain with vadd.b replacing the variable-latency operation.

latencies.notes: Data-dependent. Measured over 8 operand pairs; min 10 cycles at 0/1, max 32 cycles at 4294967295/1. The sample experiment uses the max-latency pair. Latency is derived by subtracting the same closure around vadd.b (calibration experiment).

throughput.notes: Data-dependent. CPI ranges 6 to 17 over the same operand pairs; the stored experiment uses 4294967295/1.

notes: Vector variable-latency divide/modulo. Latency 10-32 cycles and throughput CPI 6-17 are data-dependent. 32-bit lanes are not divided fully in parallel: with one slow lane the latency is 22 (vdiv.w) / 21 (xvdiv.w), and as soon as two or more lanes need many quotient bits the divider costs roughly one extra pass, giving ~32 (vdiv.w) / ~31 (xvdiv.w); the number of slow lanes beyond two does not change it further (8 slow lanes measure 31). The recorded cycles_max reflects that multi-slow-lane case. 64-bit lanes, by contrast, are fully parallel and only the slowest lane matters.
